input.quote: Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause, and shall not concern books and records relating to a period more than [***] preceding the current Calendar Year.
input.rationale: Section 9.9 is the only audit right reaching Sanofi (Section 6.9 runs the other way and benefits us, so it is not flagged). The clause already satisfies several preferred elements and those are left untouched: audits are performed by an "independent auditor of international prominence" reasonably acceptable to the audited Party (9.9(a)); the auditor and the auditing Party are bound by confidentiality (9.9(d)); and review is confined to the books and records maintained under Section 9.8, so there is no direct access to our systems. The clause nevertheless fails the fallback on its material terms because the frequency, notice period and cost-shifting underpayment threshold are all left as redacted placeholders, and the annual cap is further undercut by an open-ended "unless for cause" exception, so none of the three fallback limits is operative. Our edit inserts the fallback figures mutually - once in any Calendar Year, at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, and reimbursement only where the underpayment exceeds ten percent (10%) - and deletes the "for cause" carve-out so the cap is a hard ceiling, with no other change. Preferred-only points not pressed: no express business-hours or off-site-where-possible language.

proposal.summary: Insert express fallback audit parameters in Section 9.9: once in any Calendar Year (hard cap), fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, and cost-shifting only above a ten percent (10%) underpayment.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The audit frequency, notice period and cost-shifting threshold in Section 9.9 are left as redacted placeholders, so the limits are unenforceable as drafted. We have set them at our fallback on a mutual basis - one audit in any Calendar Year, at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, and reimbursement of audit costs only where the underpayment exceeds ten percent (10%) - and removed the open-ended "for cause" exception so the annual cap is a hard ceiling; the independent-auditor, confidentiality and records-only scope provisions are unchanged.
